```{r}
library(ggplot2)

participant_information<-read.csv("~/Downloads/GSE85307_covar-1.csv")


# Check if sample IDs match
sum(colnames(gene_expression)[-1] %in% participant_information$geoID)

# Check if probe IDs match gene names
sum(gene_expression$X %in% gene_names$PROBEID)

#  only samples that have matching participant information
matched_ids <- intersect(
  colnames(gene_expression)[-1],
  participant_information$geoID
)

# Select those samples and keep the probe ID column
expression_matched <- gene_expression[
  , c("X", matched_ids)
]

# Keep participant records in the same order as the expression samples
participant_matched <- participant_information[
  match(matched_ids, participant_information$geoID),
]

# Confirm the sample IDs are now in the same order
all(colnames(expression_matched)[-1] == participant_matched$geoID)

# Add the gene names to the expression data using probe IDs
gene_expression_named <- merge(
  gene_names,
  expression_matched,
  by.x = "PROBEID",
  by.y = "X"
)
```

```{r}
#Final submission code -CLEAN THE PARTICIPANT (COVARIATE) DATA
# In the raw file, each value is stored as text with the variable
# name in front, e.g. "mat_age_yrs: 31". R can't do math on that,
# so we remove the label and convert each column to the right type.


# Part A: remove the "name: " label from every column at once
participant_clean <- participant_matched %>%   # start from the matched participants
  mutate(                                      # mutate() changes or creates columns
    across(                                    # across() applies the same change to many columns
      -c(subjectID, geoID),                    # every column EXCEPT the two ID columns
      ~ trimws(                                # trimws() removes extra spaces at the start/end
          sub(".*: ", "",                      # sub() finds "anything followed by ': '" and replaces it with nothing
              as.character(.x))                # .x is the current column, turned into text first
        )
    )
  )
# Example: "mat_age_yrs: 31" becomes "31"
# (Still text at this point, not a number yet)

# Part B: give each column the right type
participant_clean <- participant_clean %>%
  mutate(
    # Continuous variables: turn the text "31" into the number 31
    across(c(mat_age_yrs,              # maternal age (years)
             mat_BMI,                  # maternal BMI (kg/m^2)
             mat_vitD,                 # maternal vitamin D (ng/mL)
             delivery_gestAge_wks),    # gestational age at delivery (weeks)
           as.numeric),

    # Categorical variable 1: pregnancy outcome
    # toTitleCase() capitalizes the first letter (e.g. "normal" -> "Normal")
    # so the plot labels look tidy; factor() tells R it is a category
    preg_preeclampsia = factor(tools::toTitleCase(preg_preeclampsia)),

    # Categorical variable 2: BMI category, made from continuous BMI
    # (the assignment requires one categorical variable derived
    # from a continuous one; this is it)
    BMI_category = cut(
      mat_BMI,                                   # the number we are grouping
      breaks = c(-Inf, 18.5, 25, 30, Inf),       # WHO cut-points
      labels = c("Underweight",                  # below 18.5
                 "Normal weight",                # 18.5 to under 25
                 "Overweight",                   # 25 to under 30
                 "Obesity"),                     # 30 and above
      right = FALSE                              # left edge included: BMI of exactly 25 counts as Overweight
    )
  )

#  check that the cleaning worked

# How many participants are in each outcome group?
# (should show exactly 2 groups; useNA shows any missing values)
table(participant_clean$preg_preeclampsia, useNA = "ifany")

# How many participants are in each BMI category?
table(participant_clean$BMI_category, useNA = "ifany")

# Min, mean, max etc. for each continuous variable,
# to check the numbers look realistic (e.g. ages roughly 18-45)
summary(participant_clean[, c("mat_age_yrs", "mat_BMI", "mat_vitD",
                              "delivery_gestAge_wks")])
```

```{r}



# COMBINE GENE EXPRESSION + PARTICIPANT INFO
# Goal: one table where each ROW is a participant and there is
# one COLUMN per gene (IL24, ABCA9, ABCB7), next to their
# age, BMI, outcome etc. This is the format ggplot needs.

# The three genes used for the histograms, scatterplots and boxplots
genes_of_interest <- c("IL24", "ABCA9", "ABCB7")

# Check that each gene exists in the data (should print TRUE TRUE TRUE)
genes_of_interest %in% gene_expression_named$GENE

# Reshape the expression data for these three genes
gene_wide <- gene_expression_named %>%
  filter(GENE %in% genes_of_interest) %>%   # keep only rows for our 3 genes
  select(-PROBEID) %>%                      # drop the probe ID column (we use gene names now)
  pivot_longer(-GENE,                       # turn the sample columns into rows:
               names_to = "geoID",          #   column names (sample IDs) go in "geoID"
               values_to = "expression") %>%#   the numbers go in "expression"
  group_by(GENE, geoID) %>%                 # some genes have more than one probe, so
  summarise(expression = mean(expression),  #   average them to get ONE value per gene per person
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = GENE,            # now spread back out: one column per gene
              values_from = expression)
# Result: columns geoID, ABCA9, ABCB7, IL24; one row per participant

# Attach the gene columns to the cleaned participant information,
# matching rows by the sample ID (geoID)
analysis_df <- participant_clean %>%
  left_join(gene_wide, by = "geoID")

# Remove anyone missing a variable used in the plots
n_before <- nrow(analysis_df)                    # count before removing
analysis_df <- analysis_df %>%
  filter(!is.na(preg_preeclampsia),              # must have an outcome
         !is.na(mat_age_yrs),                    # must have an age
         !is.na(BMI_category))                   # must have a BMI category
n_after <- nrow(analysis_df)                     # count after removing

# Sample sizes for the Methods section
c(initial_samples = ncol(gene_expression) - 1,   # samples in the raw expression file (minus the probe ID column)
  matched = n_before,                            # samples with matching participant info
  removed = n_before - n_after,                  # samples removed for missing data
  final = n_after)                               # final sample size

# Quick look at the first few rows of the gene columns only
head(analysis_df[, c("geoID", genes_of_interest)])









```
```{r}

#FUNCTION THAT MAKES THE 3 PLOTS FOR ANY LIST OF GENES
# Inputs:  df    = a data frame (one row per participant,
#                  one column per gene)
#          genes = a vector of gene names, e.g. c("IL24", "ABCA9")
# Output:  for each gene, a histogram, a scatterplot and a
#          boxplot, shown on screen AND saved as PDFs for LaTeX


# Make a folder called "figures" to save the plots into
# (showWarnings = FALSE means no warning if it already exists)
dir.create("figures", showWarnings = FALSE)

make_gene_plots <- function(df, genes) {

  # One shared theme so all 9 plots look the same.
  # Saving it once means we don't repeat it three times.
  my_theme <- theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5, size = 15), # bold, centered title
          axis.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),              # bold axis titles
          axis.text = element_text(size = 11, color = "black"),             # black tick labels
          legend.title = element_text(face = "bold"))                       # bold legend title

  # Loop: repeat everything inside { } once for each gene
  for (gene in genes) {

    # .data[[gene]] means "the column whose name is stored in gene".
    # On the first loop gene = "IL24", so .data[[gene]] is the IL24 column.
    # This replaces IL24_expression from your Submission 1 code.

    # ---- Plot 1: Histogram ----
    p1 <- ggplot(df, aes(x = .data[[gene]])) +
      geom_histogram(bins = 20,              # number of bars
                     fill = "#8AB9B0",       # bar color
                     color = "white",        # outline between bars
                     linewidth = 0.4,
                     na.rm = TRUE) +         # ignore missing values quietly
      labs(title = paste("Distribution of", gene, "Expression"),  # paste() builds the title from the gene name
           x = paste(gene, "Expression"),
           y = "Number of Participants") +
      my_theme

    # ---- Plot 2: Scatterplot vs maternal age ----
    p2 <- ggplot(df, aes(x = mat_age_yrs, y = .data[[gene]])) +
      geom_point(size = 2.2, alpha = 0.65,   # alpha = transparency, so overlapping points show
                 color = "#C06C84", na.rm = TRUE) +
      geom_smooth(method = "loess",          # flexible trend line
                  formula = y ~ x,           # stops R printing a message about the formula
                  se = TRUE,                 # shaded 95% confidence band
                  color = "#765285", fill = "#D9C2E9", na.rm = TRUE) +
      labs(title = paste(gene, "Expression by Maternal Age"),
           x = "Maternal Age (years)",
           y = paste(gene, "Expression")) +
      my_theme

    # ---- Plot 3: Boxplot by outcome and BMI category ----
    p3 <- ggplot(df, aes(x = preg_preeclampsia,     # x-axis: Normal vs Preeclampsia
                         y = .data[[gene]],
                         fill = BMI_category)) +    # separate colored box for each BMI group
      geom_boxplot(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8),  # boxes side by side
                   color = "#51445F", linewidth = 0.4, alpha = 0.75,
                   outlier.shape = NA,      # hide outlier dots (the points below already show them)
                   na.rm = TRUE) +
      geom_point(aes(color = BMI_category),
                 position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.15,  # spread points out a little
                                                 dodge.width = 0.8),   # line them up with their box
                 alpha = 0.55, size = 1.5, na.rm = TRUE) +
      scale_fill_manual(values = c("Underweight" = "#B8A1D9",    # box colors
                                   "Normal weight" = "#E8A0BF",
                                   "Overweight" = "#E9B872",
                                   "Obesity" = "#8AB9B0"), drop = FALSE) +
      scale_color_manual(values = c("Underweight" = "#8065A8",   # darker point colors
                                    "Normal weight" = "#B85F85",
                                    "Overweight" = "#B27A32",
                                    "Obesity" = "#4D8278"),
                         guide = "none",    # don't show a second legend for the points
                         drop = FALSE) +
      labs(title = paste(gene, "Expression by Outcome and BMI"),
           x = "Pregnancy Outcome",
           y = paste(gene, "Expression"),
           fill = "Maternal BMI\nCategory") +  # \n = line break in the legend title
      my_theme

    # Show the three plots (they appear in the knitted PDF)
    print(p1)
    print(p2)
    print(p3)

    # Save each plot as a PDF in the figures folder, e.g. figures/IL24_histogram.pdf
    ggsave(paste0("figures/", gene, "_histogram.pdf"), p1, width = 6, height = 4.5)
    ggsave(paste0("figures/", gene, "_scatter.pdf"),   p2, width = 6, height = 4.5)
    ggsave(paste0("figures/", gene, "_boxplot.pdf"),   p3, width = 7.5, height = 4.5)
  }
}

# Use the function: give it the data frame and the 3 genes
make_gene_plots(analysis_df, genes_of_interest)



```

```{r}


# SIMPLE STATISTICAL TESTS
# For each gene we ask three questions:
#  1. Is expression related to maternal AGE?        -> Spearman correlation
#  2. Is expression different between Normal and
#     Preeclampsia?                                  -> Wilcoxon rank-sum test
#  3. Is expression different across the 4 BMI
#     categories?                                    -> Kruskal-Wallis test
# These tests don't assume the data are normally distributed,
# which makes them a safe choice.
# A p-value below 0.05 is usually read as "associated".
# ---------------------------------------------------------------

#  three tests for one gene and return the results as one row
run_tests <- function(gene) {
  expr <- analysis_df[[gene]]   # the expression values for this gene

  # 1. Correlation with age: rho runs from -1 to 1
  #    (positive = goes up with age, negative = goes down, near 0 = no relationship)
  age_test <- cor.test(expr, analysis_df$mat_age_yrs,
                       method = "spearman", exact = FALSE)

  # 2. Normal vs Preeclampsia
  outcome_test <- wilcox.test(expr ~ analysis_df$preg_preeclampsia)

  # 3. Across the four BMI categories
  bmi_test <- kruskal.test(expr ~ analysis_df$BMI_category)

  # Put the results in one row, rounded to 3 decimal places
  data.frame(gene      = gene,
             rho_age   = round(age_test$estimate, 3),
             p_age     = round(age_test$p.value, 3),
             p_outcome = round(outcome_test$p.value, 3),
             p_BMI     = round(bmi_test$p.value, 3),
             row.names = NULL)
}

# Run the tests for all 3 genes and stack the rows into one table
test_results <- do.call(rbind, lapply(genes_of_interest, run_tests))
test_results


# SUMMARY STATISTICS TABLE (for LaTeX)
# Rows:    3 continuous variables (shown as mean (SD))
#          + BMI category (shown as n (%))
# Columns: Overall, Normal, Preeclampsia


# Helper 1: format a continuous variable as "mean (SD)", e.g. "26.4 (5.1)"
# sprintf() builds text from numbers; "%.1f" means 1 decimal place
mean_sd <- function(x) {
  sprintf("%.1f (%.1f)", mean(x, na.rm = TRUE), sd(x, na.rm = TRUE))
}

# Helper 2: format one category as "n (%)", e.g. "57 (36.3)"
# sum(x == lev) counts people in that category;
# mean(x == lev) gives the proportion, times 100 for a percent
n_pct <- function(x, lev) {
  sprintf("%d (%.1f)", sum(x == lev, na.rm = TRUE),
          100 * mean(x == lev, na.rm = TRUE))
}

# Helper 3: build one whole COLUMN of the table for a group of people
make_column <- function(d) {
  c(mean_sd(d$mat_age_yrs),               # row 1: age
    mean_sd(d$mat_vitD),                  # row 2: vitamin D
    mean_sd(d$delivery_gestAge_wks),      # row 3: gestational age at delivery
    "",                                   # row 4: blank (BMI heading row)
    sapply(levels(d$BMI_category),        # rows 5-8: one row per BMI category
           function(l) n_pct(d$BMI_category, l)))
}

# First column: the row labels
# "\\%" prints a % sign in LaTeX (a plain % would start a LaTeX comment)
# "\\quad" indents the BMI categories under their heading
summary_table <- data.frame(
  Characteristic = c("Maternal age (years), mean (SD)",
                     "Vitamin D (ng/mL), mean (SD)",
                     "Gestational age at delivery (weeks), mean (SD)",
                     "Maternal BMI category, n (\\%)",
                     paste0("\\quad ", levels(analysis_df$BMI_category))))

# Add the Overall column (everyone), with the sample size in the header
summary_table[[paste0("Overall (n = ", nrow(analysis_df), ")")]] <-
  make_column(analysis_df)

# Add one column per outcome group (Normal, then Preeclampsia)
for (g in levels(analysis_df$preg_preeclampsia)) {
  d <- filter(analysis_df, preg_preeclampsia == g)   # people in this group only
  summary_table[[paste0(g, " (n = ", nrow(d), ")")]] <- make_column(d)
}

# Turn the table into LaTeX code
# booktabs = TRUE gives clean publication-style lines
# escape = FALSE keeps our \\% and \\quad working
# align = "lccc": first column left-aligned, the other 3 centered
latex_table <- knitr::kable(summary_table, format = "latex",
                            booktabs = TRUE, escape = FALSE, align = "lccc")

# Save the LaTeX code to a file (uploaded to Overleaf later)
writeLines(latex_table, "table1.tex")
```

```{r}
#HEATMAP

# STEP 8a: CHOOSE AND CHECK THE 10 HEATMAP GENES
# My 3 genes + 7 other ABC transporter genes (the same gene
# family as ABCA9 and ABCB7)

heatmap_genes <- c("IL24", "ABCA9", "ABCB7",                 # my 3 genes
                   "ANKRD60", "ATG101", "CATSPERT", "ADAR",        # 7 more ABC transporters
                   "AKR1C8",  "BHMT", "CCDC87")

# Which of these genes are NOT in the data?
# character(0) means none are missing, so all 10 were found
setdiff(heatmap_genes, gene_expression_named$GENE)




# STEP 8b: HEATMAP OF 10 GENES
# Each column = one participant, each row = one gene.
# Color = how high or low a person's expression is compared with
# everyone else for that gene. Similar genes and similar people
# are grouped together (clustering). Colored bars on top show
# each person's pregnancy outcome and BMI category.


# 1. a matrix of the 10 genes (rows) x 157 participants (columns)
heat_df <- gene_expression_named %>%
  filter(GENE %in% heatmap_genes) %>%      # keep only the 10 genes
  select(-PROBEID) %>%                     # drop the probe ID column
  group_by(GENE) %>%                       # if a gene has several probes...
  summarise(across(everything(), mean))    # ...average them into one row

heat_mat <- as.matrix(heat_df[, -1])       # numbers only (drop the GENE column)
rownames(heat_mat) <- heat_df$GENE         # use gene names as row names
heat_mat <- heat_mat[, analysis_df$geoID]  # same participants, same order as analysis_df

dim(heat_mat)                              # should print 10 157

# 2. Tracking bars: one row per participant, one column per categorical variable
#    row.names must be the geoIDs so pheatmap can match bars to columns
annotation <- data.frame(
  "Pregnancy Outcome" = analysis_df$preg_preeclampsia,
  "BMI Category"      = analysis_df$BMI_category,
  row.names   = analysis_df$geoID,
  check.names = FALSE)                     # keeps the spaces in the column names

# 3. Colors for the tracking bars (the BMI colors match the boxplots)
annotation_colors <- list(
  "Pregnancy Outcome" = c("Normal" = "#9CB4CC", "Preeclampsia" = "#C06C84"),
  "BMI Category"      = c("Underweight" = "#B8A1D9", "Normal weight" = "#E8A0BF",
                          "Overweight" = "#E9B872", "Obesity" = "#8AB9B0"))

# 4. Draw the heatmap
heatmap_plot <- pheatmap(
  heat_mat,
  scale = "row",                          # z-score each gene so all genes share one color scale
  clustering_distance_rows = "euclidean", # how similarity between genes is measured
  clustering_distance_cols = "euclidean", # how similarity between participants is measured
  clustering_method = "complete",         # how clusters are joined together
  annotation_col = annotation,            # the tracking bars on top
  annotation_colors = annotation_colors,
  show_colnames = FALSE,                  # hide 157 sample IDs (unreadable anyway)
  color = colorRampPalette(c("#3B6E8F", "white", "#B5485D"))(100), # blue = low, red = high
  breaks = seq(-3, 3, length.out = 101),  # cap colors at +/- 3 so outliers don't wash out the rest
  border_color = NA,                      # no grid lines between cells
  main = "Expression of 10 Genes by Pregnancy Outcome and BMI")

# 5. Save the heatmap as a PDF in the figures folder
pdf("figures/heatmap.pdf", width = 8, height = 5.5)  # open a PDF file
grid::grid.draw(heatmap_plot$gtable)                 # draw the heatmap into it
dev.off()                                            # close and save the file







```
```{r}



#additional plot 

# DUMBBELL PLOT 
# For each of the 10 heatmap genes: the mean expression in Normal
# vs Preeclampsia pregnancies, joined by a bar. Genes are z-scored
# so all 10 share the same scale, and they are sorted by how big
# the difference between groups is.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------

#  Z-score each gene (mean 0, SD 1 across all participants)
#    scale() works on columns, so we flip (t) the matrix, scale, then flip back
z_mat <- t(scale(t(heat_mat)))

# 2. Mean and 95% confidence interval for each gene in each group
group_means <- as.data.frame(t(z_mat)) %>%            # rows = participants, columns = genes
  mutate(group = analysis_df$preg_preeclampsia) %>%   # add each person's outcome
  pivot_longer(-group, names_to = "gene",             # long format: one row per person per gene
               values_to = "z") %>%
  group_by(gene, group) %>%                           # for each gene in each group...
  summarise(mean_z = mean(z),                         # ...the mean
            se = sd(z) / sqrt(n()),                   # ...the standard error
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(lower = mean_z - 1.96 * se,                  # lower end of the 95% CI
         upper = mean_z + 1.96 * se)                  # upper end of the 95% CI

# One row per gene with both group means side by side (used for the grey bar)
gene_gaps <- group_means %>%
  select(gene, group, mean_z) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = group, values_from = mean_z) %>%  # columns: gene, Normal, Preeclampsia
  mutate(difference = Preeclampsia - Normal) %>%             # size of the gap between groups
  arrange(difference)                                        # sort genes by the gap

#  Keep the genes in that sorted order on the y-axis
group_means$gene <- factor(group_means$gene, levels = gene_gaps$gene)
gene_gaps$gene   <- factor(gene_gaps$gene,   levels = gene_gaps$gene)

# Draw the plot (layers are added from back to front)
plot_dumbbell <- ggplot() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed",     # dashed line at 0 = overall average
             color = "grey60") +
  geom_segment(data = gene_gaps,                      # grey bar joining the two group means
               aes(x = Normal, xend = Preeclampsia, y = gene, yend = gene),
               linewidth = 1.6, color = "grey80") +
  geom_errorbar(data = group_means,                   # 95% CI whiskers
                aes(xmin = lower, xmax = upper, y = gene, color = group),
                width = 0.25, orientation = "y") +
  geom_point(data = group_means,                      # the mean dots
             aes(x = mean_z, y = gene, color = group), size = 3.5) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Normal" = "#3B6E8F",
                                "Preeclampsia" = "#C06C84")) +
  labs(title = "Mean Gene Expression by Pregnancy Outcome",
       x = "Mean Expression (z-score, 95% CI)",
       y = NULL,                                      # gene names are self-explanatory
       color = "Pregnancy Outcome") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5, size = 15),
        axis.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
        axis.text = element_text(size = 11, color = "black"),
        legend.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
        legend.position = "bottom")

#  Show the plot and save it for LaTeX
print(plot_dumbbell)
ggsave("figures/dumbbell.pdf", plot_dumbbell, width = 7, height = 5)

#  The differences, sorted (useful for writing the Results)
gene_gaps




```
